title: The beginning of the good news

sources: Mark 1:1 (“The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God”)
Mark 1:4-6 (John baptizing in the wilderness, preaching repentance; clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt)
Mark 1:5 (all the country of Judea and all of Jerusalem went out to him and were baptized in the Jordan)
Mark 1:7 (“After me comes he who is mightier than I”)
Mark 1:9-11 (Jesus from Nazareth is baptized; the heavens torn open, the Spirit descending like a dove; “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased”)
Matthew 3:14 (John tries to stop him), behind one wrong option only
Mark 8:27-31 and Mark 11 (the road toward Jerusalem)
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized
check: Scholars debate whether Mark 1:1 (“the beginning”) titles the whole book or only the opening; the lesson says “many readers” take it for the whole book. Confirm wording.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever wanted to start reading the bible and not known where to begin?
options: then i’ve got a good place for you. it starts at a river.
most people have. this one is short and fast.
good. let’s read its first page with fresh eyes.

steps.line: The shortest of the four gospels doesn’t start with a manger. It starts, “The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ.”
steps.label: Mark 1:1

steps.line: In the desert by the Jordan River, a wild prophet named John, dressed in camel’s hair, called people to turn back to God.
steps.label: Mark 1:4-6

steps.line: Crowds came from Jerusalem and all the countryside, and he baptized them in the river.
steps.label: Mark 1:5

steps.line: “Someone is coming after me who is greater than I am,” John said. Then one day Jesus came from Nazareth, and was baptized too.
steps.label: Mark 1:7-9

steps.q: As Jesus comes up out of the water, what do you guess happens?
o: John kneels to him in front of everyone
Nothing; he walks off with the crowd
The sky tears open and a voice speaks
steps.why: The sky tears open. Mark’s word is strong: not opened, torn.

steps.line: As he came up out of the water, the sky tore open and the Spirit came down on him like a dove. And a voice spoke.
steps.label: Mark 1:10

steps.q: Mark uses that verb, “torn,” just once more in his gospel. Where?
o: The temple curtain, as Jesus dies
steps.why: At the cross the temple curtain is torn top to bottom, and a soldier says, “Truly this man was God’s Son.” Torn sky, beloved Son; torn curtain, God’s Son.

steps.q: Jesus hasn’t taught or healed anyone yet, and already he hears “beloved.” Why might the gospel start here?
o: Love comes first, before anything is earned
To prove to the crowd who he was
To show he was greater than John
steps.why: In Mark the voice says “You are,” spoken to Jesus himself, not announced to the crowd. Before any work, he hears he’s loved.

steps.line: From there the story runs. “Immediately” comes again and again, on a road that leads all the way to Jerusalem.
steps.label: Mark 1:12; 11:1

steps.q: Mark’s favourite word is “immediately.” About how often does it appear in his short gospel?
steps.why: Over 40 times (Greek euthys). No birth story, no slow start: Mark tells it at a run, on a road toward Jerusalem.

say: here’s what i love. mark’s very first word is “beginning.” many readers hear it this way: the good news isn’t finished when the book ends.

christians believe they’re invited into it, baptized as jesus was, into a life that starts with being loved. many churches baptize babies, others baptize believers who choose it. both see it as a beginning.

steps.q: Mark opens with “the beginning of the good news,” and many readers take that for the whole book. What might that suggest?
o: He planned to write a second book
The story keeps going in its readers
He ran out of time to finish it
steps.why: Mark ends abruptly, at an empty tomb. If the book is the beginning, the rest is still being written, by the people who pick it up.

today.say: start here. mark’s gospel is short enough to read in one evening. read or listen to its first chapter today, about ten minutes. watch, learn, or join in: your choice.
options: good. it moves fast. you’ll be at the sea of galilee in no time.
perfect. it was first heard out loud anyway.
